clue.text: Nicholas Serota's on board, displaying quality desirable in 13

indicators.note: to be on board is to be aboard, so the man's possessive phrase sits within the vessel's word

parts.note: board here is a vessel you can go aboard, a ship
Sir Nicholas Serota ran London's Tate galleries, so he is the Tate's man, and the 's makes it TATE'S MAN'S

explanation.surface: A gallery director has joined a company board and shows a quality a head of state ought to have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' plays two parts: board gives the vessel and on says the possessive phrase goes aboard it. The 13 is a cross-reference to 13 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in guiding public affairs wisely is the very virtue one hopes for in a head of state.

clue.text: In sh*t, rolled joints, getting no appreciation

indicators.note: In tells us the joints are placed within the reversed letters of the starred word
rolled means the word is turned over, so its letters read backwards

parts.note: the starred word as printed supplies the letters S, H and T
ankles are joints of the leg

explanation.surface: Someone in a mess, rolling joints of cannabis, gets no thanks for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled' turns the censored word round to THS before the joints go in. The asterisk only censors it; just the three printed letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that wins no gratitude is called a thankless one, an everyday idiom.

clue.text: She does her best in German city

definitions.meaning: a person who keeps making an effort, one who tries
An old Roman city on the Moselle in western Germany

explanation.surface: A woman giving her all in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tries hard is a trier; Trier is also the Rhineland-Palatinate city on the Moselle.

clue.text: Places left in a mess by surgical instrument

indicators.note: in a mess says the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An operating theatre where things are left untidy by a surgeon's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, very sharp blade is the knife a surgeon uses for cutting during operations.

clue.text: Old flame on the rebound splits leading part of weapon

indicators.note: splits means the reversed former partner breaks into the word for leading

parts.note: ahead means in front, leading

indicators.note: on the rebound means bouncing back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: an ex is a former lover, an old flame

explanation.surface: A former lover, on the rebound, splits up with someone at the head of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rebound' reads like heartbreak but is the reversal signal, giving XE.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy cutting blade of a chopping tool is one component of the hatchet or battleaxe as a weapon.

clue.text: Still maintaining first figure

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the word for still keeps the other inside it

parts.note: static means still, not moving
1st, written as IST, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: Someone still keeping their first figure, a slim shape kept over years.
explanation.walkthrough: IST is 1st with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A single numerical datum, such as a percentage, is a figure in the numbers sense.

clue.text: Some complain an examiner's stupid

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people grumble that an examiner is dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or senseless remarks are described as stupid or witless, a plain synonym.

clue.text: 8 hot brides died suspiciously — she gets the lot

indicators.note: suspiciously suggests something fishy, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the number 8 is spelt out as the word eight, hot is H as on a tap, brides stays as written, and died is D as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Eight hot brides have died in suspicious circumstances: a dark murder plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 8 is not a cross-reference to another light; it is simply the number spelt out as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: At an auction the bidder offering most money wins, taking the lot under the hammer.

clue.text: Composing Thistle with Two Eggs, crack up

indicators.note: composing means putting together, so the letters are arranged afresh
Two means the egg is taken twice

parts.note: a single egg gives the letters, used twice

explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is an idiom for bursting into helpless laughter, which is fits of giggling.

clue.text: 1 dull 7 outside, devoid of life

indicators.note: outside says the answer to 7 goes round the other pieces

parts.note: 7 points to the answer of 7 Down
the digit 1 is read as the letter I
mat, also spelt matt, means dull, not shiny

explanation.surface: A dull, stupid thing with no life in it, like a numbered list of insults.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without life, such as a stone, is lifeless in the plainest sense.

clue.text: Conscious of a send-off

parts.note: a wake is the gathering that gives the dead a send-off

explanation.surface: Being aware of a farewell party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conscious of' reads as one phrase, but 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone conscious is not asleep, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: One grand received by female rambler

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a female
the Roman numeral I is one
K, short for kilo, is a thousand pounds, a grand

explanation.surface: A woman is given a thousand pounds by a lady out walking.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is someone who walks in the countryside for pleasure, a synonym.

clue.text: Leader's gift including driving licence, say

indicators.note: including means the gift holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a present is a gift
a driving licence is an example of ID, identification

explanation.surface: A leader's present is a driving licence, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of state or head of an organisation is its leader.

clue.text: Artist's guide confused clients

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter's instructions have left the customers baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-out template guides an artist painting letters or patterns, a fair description.

clue.text: Drink, for little money, source of true river water in France

parts.note: a coin is a small piece of money

indicators.note: source of means the first letter, where the word starts

parts.note: eau is the French for water

explanation.surface: A cheap drink: true river water from a French source.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur, so it is one example of a drink.

clue.text: Of a certain age, but worth going out with?

definitions.meaning: able to be assigned a date, having a determinable age
attractive enough to be taken on a date

explanation.surface: A middle-aged person who might still be worth a romantic evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of a certain age' usually means middle-aged; here it means an age can be fixed for the object.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from date: an artefact whose age can be established, and a person suitable for romance.

clue.text: Woody matter in cheese getting bishop unduly upset

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: too means unduly, excessively

explanation.surface: A bishop gets far too upset over some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard root wood of the heath tree is what tobacco pipes are carved from, so it is woody material.

clue.text: Go downhill, dividing illicit payment for performing illicitly

indicators.note: dividing means the downhill word splits the payment word in two

parts.note: a bung is a bribe, an illicit payment
to ski is to go downhill on skis

explanation.surface: A bribe-taking skier making unlicensed appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNG is British slang for a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing music in the street for money, often without a licence, is street performing of that kind.

clue.text: Leave, receiving directions to bug secret service

indicators.note: receiving means the word for leave takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: to go is to leave
E and S are compass directions, east and south
to tap a phone is to bug it

explanation.surface: A spy is told to leave after being given orders to bug a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was Nazi Germany's secret state police, an example of a secret service.

clue.text: Composer turning up volume in Italy

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetres, is a measure of volume
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A composer turning up the volume in Italy.

explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Puccini wrote the operas La Bohème and Tosca, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: After gym, theologian was first to get flogged

parts.note: PE, physical education, is gym at school
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
led means was first, was in front

explanation.definitionFit: To flog something is informal British for selling it, and hawked goods are sold door to door.

clue.text: Stood in, backing exercise in action

parts.note: a sit-up is a stomach exercise

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acted as a substitute for another has stood in, a synonym.

clue.text: Heathen page once more dropping one

parts.note: again means once more
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.definitionFit: A heathen holds no mainstream religion, and pagan is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Maybe son gets Grand Old Party (Republican) revived

indicators.note: revived means brought back in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party

explanation.surface: A son joins the Republican Party and gives it new life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'son' does double duty: it gives S to the anagram and is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprog is British slang for a child, and a son is one example.

clue.text: Staged demonstration in silk

definitions.meaning: a protest that has been held, a sit-in in the past tense
a smooth glossy fabric woven from silk

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

clue.text: Parcel out executioner's equipment: it comes in various forms

parts.note: to allot is to parcel out shares
a hangman uses a rope

explanation.surface: Handing out the hangman's gear, which is available in several kinds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: an allotrope is one of several forms of an element, as diamond and graphite are of carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Elements such as carbon exist in different structural forms, each one named that way in chemistry.

clue.text: Disregarding instructions, excessive loan's accepted

parts.note: inordinate means excessive
